html:
The Tututni are one of the Lower Rogue River Athabaskan peoples of southwestern Oregon, who lived in villages along the lower Rogue River and its branches near the Pacific coast. They speak an Athabaskan language.

They fished for salmon, gathered acorns and camas, and hunted. Gold miners and settlers poured into the region in the 1850s, and fighting broke out in the Rogue River Wars of 1855 and 1856. The Tututni signed the Coast Treaty of 1855 and were then moved north to the Siletz reservation; their descendants belong to the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians. Their neighbours included the Coquille.
